Developer Level 2 — Advanced Track Enhancing the Customer Complaints Application This track does not build a new application. Every session goes back into the SAME Customer Complaints app built in Developer Level 1, and layers a new advanced capability onto it — the same end-to-end build approach used in the Level 1 guide. Prerequisite: Developer Level 1 completion is mandatory. Proposed dates are placeholders (one session per working day, starting Mon 07 Sep 2026) — confirm actual start date and cadence.

Developer Level 1 was built as an end-to-end project: one real application — the Customer Complaints Application — built up session by session. This Level 2 guide follows the same approach: no new application is created. Every session below re-opens the entities, pages, entity files, and controllers already built in Level 1 and extends them with an advanced capability, so trainees see how real applications evolve rather than practicing features in isolation. Topics are drawn from the Training Topics sheet, filtered to entries tagged “Developer Level 2,” and mapped onto concrete enhancements of the existing app. Tool names use the current naming glossary, with legacy names noted where relevant.

Sessions must be taken in order — each session's steps assume the previous session's enhancement is already in place, exactly as in the Level 1 guide. Session Date Topic Area Application Enhancement Session 1 Mon, 07 Sep 2026 Advanced BOL & Data Modelling Network Modes — Offline-Ready Properties · Sort Order & Entity Index · Entity Rules — Auto-Escalation on Update · Query Rules — Role-Based Field Masking · BOL Transaction — Close Complaint with Feedback Session 2 Tue, 08 Sep 2026 Advanced Page Builder & Client-Side Debugging Embedded Section — Complaint Timeline · Advanced kloControls · TransNode onArrive & navigateId · Server-Side Debugging & Auto Update Data Session 3 Wed, 09 Sep 2026 Security, Permissions & Data Access Design-Time Permissions · Row Wise Auth · Data Access Rules & User Access Summary · Role Permissions (Runtime) & Permission Logs Session 4 Thu, 10 Sep 2026 Offline, Middleware & Bulk Data Local Archive · Initial Downloads · Middleware — Device & SAP · KloSectionXlsx — Bulk Customer Import Session 5 Fri, 11 Sep 2026 Workflows, Scheduling & Notifications Escalation Approval Workflow · Scheduler — Nightly SLA Sweep · Notifications · deeplink & Banner Session 6 Mon, 14 Sep 2026 Reporting — Charts & Pivot Modeller kloChart — Status Breakdown · Advanced Chart — TAT Trend · Pivot Modeller Session 7 Tue, 15 Sep 2026 Monitoring & Troubleshooting Scheduler & Log Monitoring · Notification & Queue Monitoring · APK/IPA & Query Console Session 8 Wed, 16 Sep 2026 App Management, Branding & Deployment App Inheritance & Modification · Customer Branding · Git Repo & Active Sessions · App Migration to QA
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 Duration: Full day Topics: BOL, Data Modelling

Configure Network Modes so offline-relevant properties sync correctly to field devices. Apply Sort Order and an Entity Index to d_complaints for performance and predictable ordering. Extend the existing Entity Rules with a new auto-escalation rule. Extend the existing Query Rules with role-based field masking. Build a BOL Transaction that commits two entities atomically. What This Session Builds On Developer Level 1 (Sessions 1–5) built d_complaints with its properties, one Entity Rule (onCreateComplaint) and one Query Rule (beforeQ) on q_complaints. This session does not start a new entity — it goes back into the same d_complaints and q_complaints files and adds the advanced BOL capabilities on top.

A field IT Team member on a tablet needs complaint status and priority visible even with no signal, while internal notes stay server-side only. Meanwhile complaints are quietly sailing past SLA with no auto-flag, and a support rep spots that anyone on the IT Team can see a customer's full contact details in the list — details they never needed for their job.

Not every property should sync to a field device the same way. Configure Network Mode per property on d_complaints. # Action Detail 1 Open properties Procify Data Studio → d_complaints → Properties tab. 2 Restrict remark Set Network Mode = Online Only on remark — internal notes should not be cached on IT Team field devices. 3 Always sync core fields Set Network Mode = Always on complaint_id, s_status, priority so they remain visible even when the device is offline. 4 Save & update schema Save, then Update Schema, and confirm no errors.
documents.s: Part A — Network Modes — Offline-Ready Properties

documents.t: The complaints list currently has no defined default order and no index for the fields it is filtered on most. # Action Detail 1 Set Sort Order On priority: custom order CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW. On created_on: DESCENDING as the secondary sort. 2 Create Entity Index Entity Index tab → Add → ID: idx_complaint_status_priority — fields: s_status, priority. 3 Update Schema Update Schema and verify the index is listed under the entity's Test → Data Browser diagnostics.
documents.s: Part B — Sort Order & Entity Index

documents.t: Reopen the same d_complaints.ts file from Level 1 Session 5 and add a second rule alongside onCreateComplaint. # Action Detail 1 Register the rule Rule tab → Add → Event Type: On Update | Channel: Always on Server | Clazz: this | Invocation Method: checkEscalation. 2 Implement checkEscalation If s_status is OPEN or INPROCESS and (today − created_on) > 3 days, set is_escalated = true. 3 Test Backdate a test record's created_on in Data Browser to 4 days ago, save, and confirm is_escalated flips to true.
documents.s: Part C — Entity Rules — Auto-Escalation on Update

documents.t: Extend q_complaints.ts — the same file where beforeQ was written in Level 1 Session 4 — with an afterQ rule. # Action Detail 1 Add afterQ Event Type: After Query. In the handler, if the requesting role is IT_TEAM, replace customer contact fields in each result row with ‘•••’. 2 Test as IT Team Log in as it_<prid> — confirm customer contact fields are masked in the list. 3 Test as Manager Log in as mgr_<prid> — confirm the same fields show full data.
documents.s: Part D — Query Rules — Role-Based Field Masking

documents.t: Combine a status update and a new voice record into one atomic operation. # Action Detail 1 Create the transaction Data Studio → new BOL Transaction Tx_CloseWithFeedback, covering d_complaints (update s_status = CLOSED) and d_complaint_voices (create feedback record). 2 Wire the button Add a ‘Close with Feedback’ action on s_detail_header that commits both TransNodes through this transaction. 3 Test atomicity Force the voice record to fail validation (e.g. leave it blank) and confirm the status change also rolls back — not just the voice record. Session 1 Checkpoint ✔ Network Modes verified in an offline emulation for at least 3 properties. ✔ s_complaints defaults to priority order; idx_complaint_status_priority exists and is used. ✔ checkEscalation rule fires correctly on a backdated test record. ✔ afterQ masks customer fields for IT_TEAM but not for Manager. ✔ Tx_CloseWithFeedback commits both entities together or rolls back together. Enhancement delivered: Extends the existing d_complaints / q_complaints files from Level 1 (not a new entity) with offline sync control, performance indexing, automatic SLA escalation, field-level data masking by role, and an atomic close-with-feedback commit.
documents.s: Part E — BOL Transaction — Close Complaint with Feedback

documents.t: Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 Duration: Full day
documents.s: Session 2 — Advanced Page Builder & Client-Side Debugging

documents.t: Build a reusable Embedded Section and use it on two different pages. Add Advanced kloControls (rating, file uploader) to the detail screen. Configure TransNode onArrive and navigateId behaviour. Debug the Session 1 server-side rule using Server-Side Debugging. Enable Auto Update Data so the Manager's list refreshes without manual action. What This Session Builds On p_complaints was built manually in Level 1 Session 2 and styled in Session 6; p_complaint_dashboard was built in Session 5. Both existing pages are extended here — no new page is created from scratch.

A Manager opens a complaint and has to hunt across screens to see whether this customer has complained before. A rep marks a complaint resolved but there's no way to capture how satisfied the customer actually was, or attach a photo of a damaged product without emailing it separately.

Build one timeline section and reuse it in two places. # Action Detail 1 Create the section New section s_complaint_timeline (screenType: timeline) bound to a TransNode combining voices and status-change history. 2 Embed in detail In pa_comp_details, add a new section, mark it Embedded, and point its source to s_complaint_timeline. 3 Reuse on dashboard Add the same embedded section to p_complaint_dashboard as a ‘Recent Activity’ panel — confirming true cross-page reuse.
documents.s: Part A — Embedded Section — Complaint Timeline

documents.t: Add two controls that were not covered in Level 1's basic control set. # Action Detail 1 Add kloRating On s_detail_header, add a kloRating control bound to a new transient property t_satisfaction_score, visible only when s_status = CLOSED. 2 Add kloFileUploader On the attachments section, add kloFileUploader bound to the d_complaints_attachment relation built in Level 1. 3 Full Preview Confirm the rating control only appears on closed complaints and the uploader stores a file record correctly.

Make the detail screen smarter about what loads automatically and where links resolve to. # Action Detail 1 Configure onArrive On the detail TransNode, set onArrive to auto-load the 5 most recent related voices — no extra click required. 2 Configure navigateId On the ticket_id link control, set navigateId so it always resolves to pa_complaint_details, whether clicked from p_complaints or the dashboard's embedded timeline. 3 Test both entry points Click a complaint from the main list, then from the dashboard timeline — confirm both land on the same detail area correctly populated.

Debug the rule written in Session 1 and make the Manager's grid self-refreshing. # Action Detail 1 Attach debugger Set a breakpoint inside checkEscalation in VS Code and attach to the running Private Node. 2 Step through Trigger a save on a test complaint and step through the rule execution line by line. 3 Enable auto refresh On s_complaints, set Auto Update Data = true with a 30-second interval. 4 Verify Create a complaint as Employee in one browser tab; confirm it appears in the Manager's grid within 30 seconds without a manual refresh. Session 2 Checkpoint ✔ s_complaint_timeline renders correctly on both p_complaints and p_complaint_dashboard. ✔ kloRating and kloFileUploader function as specified. ✔ onArrive auto-loads voices; navigateId resolves correctly from both entry points. ✔ Breakpoint debugging confirmed inside checkEscalation. ✔ Manager's grid auto-refreshes within 30 seconds of a new complaint being created. Enhancement delivered: Adds a reusable complaint-history timeline, a satisfaction rating and attachment capture on resolution, smarter auto-loading/navigation, and a self-refreshing Manager grid — all on the existing pages built in Level 1.
documents.s: Part D — Server-Side Debugging & Auto Update Data

documents.t: Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 Duration: Full day

Enforce CRUD restrictions server-side using design-time Permissions. Restrict IT Team visibility to their own team's complaints using Row Wise Auth. Scope customer data by region using Data Access Rules. Audit a user's effective access using User Access Summary. Grant, use, and revoke a temporary elevated Role Permission, and confirm it in Permission Logs. What This Session Builds On Level 1 Session 7 hid or disabled buttons per role using Vienable — a UI-level control only. This session enforces the same rules at the platform/security level so they hold even if a user calls the API directly.

An IT Team member who left last month still has delete rights if they call the API directly, even though the button is hidden in the UI. A regional manager can see every customer's complaints nationwide instead of just their region, and after an override was granted during an incident, nobody can say who approved it or when it was revoked.

Configure real CRUD restrictions, not just hidden buttons. # Action Detail 1 Configure Employee Employee role: Create + Read only. 2 Configure Manager Manager role: Create + Read + Update + Delete. 3 Configure IT Team IT Team role: Read + Update only. 4 Test server-side block Log in as emp_<prid> and confirm Delete is blocked even if attempted outside the hidden button (e.g. via a direct API call).

Restrict IT Team to only the complaints assigned to their own team. # Action Detail 1 Configure the rule Row Wise Auth on d_complaints: IT_TEAM role only receives rows where responsible_team = current user's team. 2 Test Log in as it_<prid> — confirm only assigned complaints appear, even via direct navigation to a different complaint's URL.

Scope customer master data regionally and verify it. # Action Detail 1 Create the rule New Data Access Rule scoping d_customers by region. 2 Assign to Manager Assign the rule to mgr_<prid> for their region. 3 Verify with User Access Summary Open User Access Summary for mgr_<prid> and confirm the rule and effective permissions are listed correctly.
documents.s: Part C — Data Access Rules & User Access Summary

documents.t: Simulate an incident requiring temporary elevated access, then audit it. # Action Detail 1 Grant temporary access Create a runtime Role Permission override allowing IT_TEAM_LEAD to Delete during an incident. 2 Use and revoke Apply, test the elevated Delete, then revoke the override. 3 Audit in Permission Logs Confirm both the grant and the revoke appear in Permission Logs with timestamp and actor. Session 3 Checkpoint ✔ CRUD restrictions enforced server-side for all 3 roles. ✔ IT Team row-level filtering confirmed, including via direct URL access. ✔ Data Access Rule created, assigned, and confirmed via User Access Summary. ✔ Temporary Role Permission granted, used, revoked, and fully audited in Permission Logs. Enhancement delivered: Replaces Level 1's UI-only button hiding (Vienable) with rules enforced at the platform/security level, restricts IT Team visibility to assigned complaints, scopes customer data by region, and closes the audit gap on temporary access.
documents.s: Part D — Role Permissions (Runtime) & Permission Logs

documents.t: Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 Duration: Full day

Enable offline access to assigned complaints for field IT Team users via Local Archive. Reduce first-login sync payload using Initial Downloads. Push closed complaints to an external SAP system via Middleware. Bulk-import customer master data using KloSectionXlsx. What This Session Builds On The application has only worked online through Sessions 1–3. This session makes it usable by IT Team members working onsite without connectivity, and adds a bulk-data path for customer onboarding.

An IT Team technician visiting a customer site with no signal can't pull up the complaint they're there to resolve. Every login re-downloads the full complaint history instead of just what's assigned, closed complaints aren't reaching the SAP billing system automatically, and onboarding 20 new customers means entering each one by hand.

Keep a working slice of data on the device for offline use. # Action Detail 1 Configure archive scope Local Archive on d_complaints and d_complaint_voices for the IT_TEAM role — retain the last 30 days of assigned complaints on-device. 2 Test offline On a device/emulator, disconnect network and confirm assigned complaints and their voice history are still viewable.

Reduce what gets pulled on first login. # Action Detail 1 Configure the download set Only OPEN/INPROCESS complaints assigned to the logging-in IT Team user are included in the first sync — not full history. 2 Verify Time a fresh login before and after the change and confirm a smaller payload.

Integrate with an external billing system. # Action Detail 1 Configure the channel New Middleware channel that pushes CLOSED complaints to an external SAP endpoint for billing reconciliation. 2 Test Close a test complaint and confirm the outbound payload appears in the middleware queue.

Add Excel-based bulk operations to the customer master entity. # Action Detail 1 Add to d_customers Attach KloSectionXlsx to the customer section, enabling bulk Excel upload/download. 2 Bulk import Prepare a sample sheet of 20 customers and import via the section. 3 Verify Confirm all 20 records land correctly in Data Browser. Session 4 Checkpoint ✔ IT Team can view assigned complaints and voice history fully offline. ✔ Initial download payload measurably reduced and verified. ✔ One closed complaint confirmed pushed to the SAP middleware queue. ✔ 20 customers successfully bulk-imported via KloSectionXlsx. Enhancement delivered: Makes the app usable in the field without connectivity, shrinks the first-login sync payload, automates the SAP billing hand-off on closure, and adds bulk customer onboarding.
documents.s: Part D — KloSectionXlsx — Bulk Customer Import

documents.t: Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 Duration: Full day

Route escalated complaints through a Manager approval Workflow. Add a nightly Scheduled Task as a server-side safety net for SLA breaches. Notify the right people by Email, SMS, and In-App at the right moments. Deep-link notification emails directly into the relevant complaint. Configure an app-wide Banner for planned maintenance. What This Session Builds On Session 1 added a server-side is_escalated flag. This session adds the human workflow and communication layer that reacts to it.

A complaint sits open for a week past SLA with no one following up, because there's no approval step and no nightly check catching it. A customer is never told their complaint was resolved unless someone remembers to call, and a support email can't deep-link straight to the complaint it's about.

Give escalation a human decision point. # Action Detail 1 Build the workflow When is_escalated becomes true, route an approval task to the Manager to confirm reassignment of responsible_team. 2 Test Trigger escalation on a test complaint and confirm the Manager receives the task in Pending Approvals.

Add a server-side safety net independent of individual saves. # Action Detail 1 Create the task Scheduled Task that runs nightly, re-checking all OPEN/INPROCESS complaints against the 3-day SLA rule from Session 1. 2 Run manually and verify Trigger once via Running Tasks and confirm overdue complaints are correctly flagged.
documents.s: Part B — Scheduler — Nightly SLA Sweep

documents.t: Close the communication loop for assignment and resolution. # Action Detail 1 Assignment email Email notification to responsible_team the moment a complaint is assigned. 2 Resolution in-app alert In-App notification to the originating Employee when status changes to CLOSED. 3 Verify delivery Trigger both scenarios and confirm delivery in Notification History.

Make notifications actionable and announce planned downtime. # Action Detail 1 Configure deeplink The assignment email's ‘View Complaint’ link opens directly to the correct complaint detail screen. 2 Configure Banner App-wide banner announcing a planned maintenance window, visible to all roles for 24 hours. Session 5 Checkpoint ✔ Escalation approval task correctly routed to and actionable by the Manager. ✔ Nightly scheduler flags overdue complaints on a manual run. ✔ Assignment email and resolution in-app alert both confirmed delivered in Notification History. ✔ Deeplink opens the exact correct complaint; banner visible to all 3 roles. Enhancement delivered: Adds a human approval step on escalation, a nightly check independent of individual saves, closes the communication loop on assignment/resolution, and makes notifications actionable.
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 Duration: Full day

Replace static dashboard tiles with a live kloChart. Build an advanced TAT trend chart over a rolling 30-day window. Build a Pivot Modeller report for cross-team, cross-type analysis. What This Session Builds On Level 1 Session 5 built p_complaint_dashboard with static status-count tiles fed by status_count_query. This session replaces and extends those same tiles with real charts.

A Manager glances at the dashboard and sees numbers that were already stale this morning, with no way to see the SLA trend over the last month or drill into which team is falling behind — only static totals.

Turn the existing tile counts into a live chart. # Action Detail 1 Add the chart Add a kloChart bar chart to p_complaint_dashboard bound to the existing status_count_query TransNode. 2 Cross-check and replace Verify the chart's counts match the old static tiles, then remove the tiles.

Add a second, more advanced chart tracking service-level performance. # Action Detail 1 Build the query New query aggregating actual_tat vs standard_tat by week for the last 30 days. 2 Configure the chart Advanced line chart with two series (actual vs standard) and custom axis formatting.
documents.s: Part B — Advanced Chart — TAT Trend

documents.t: Give Managers a drillable cross-tab report. # Action Detail 1 Build the pivot Rows = complaint_type, Columns = responsible_team, Values = count of complaints, Filter = current month. 2 Publish & verify Publish to the EAM Portal and confirm a Manager can drill into a specific cell to see the underlying records. Session 6 Checkpoint ✔ Static dashboard tiles fully replaced by a live kloChart with matching counts. ✔ TAT trend chart renders 30 days of actual-vs-standard data. ✔ Pivot report published to EAM Portal and drill-down verified. Enhancement delivered: Replaces static dashboard tiles with live, trend-aware reporting and adds a drillable cross-tab view for Managers.
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 Duration: Full day

Diagnose a simulated scheduler failure end-to-end using platform monitoring tools. Confirm notification delivery and resolve a stuck offline sync record. Confirm the SAP middleware payload was processed via Legacy Queue Monitoring. Trace a native control rendering issue on a built APK. Independently verify dashboard numbers using Query Console. What This Session Builds On The app is feature-complete after Sessions 1–6 (automation, offline sync, integrations, reporting). This session is entirely about operating and troubleshooting what was built, not adding new features.

The nightly SLA sweep silently failed last night and nobody noticed until complaints started piling up unflagged. A customer insists they never got a resolution notification, and there's no way to check; finance says a closed complaint never showed up in SAP and nobody can tell whether it's stuck or lost.

Break the Session 5 scheduler on purpose, then find and fix it. # Action Detail 1 Simulate a failure Introduce a bad condition into the nightly SLA-sweep task and trigger it. 2 Observe the failure Confirm the failure appears in Scheduler Monitoring and Task History. 3 Trace the root cause Find the underlying error in Google Logs. 4 Fix and re-run Correct the task and confirm success via Running Tasks.

Confirm the Session 4 and 5 integrations are actually working end-to-end. # Action Detail 1 Verify notifications Check Notification History for the assignment/resolution messages from Session 5 — confirm delivered status. 2 Diagnose a stuck sync Simulate a stuck offline record on Server Queue / Mobile Sync Queue for an IT Team device from Session 4, and resolve it. 3 Check the SAP channel Review Legacy Queue Monitoring to confirm the Session 4 closed-complaint payload to SAP was processed.

Trace a native rendering issue and cross-verify reporting data. # Action Detail 1 Build and test the APK Build a debug APK including the kloRating control from Session 2. 2 Debug if needed If the control fails to render natively, use APK/IPA debugging tools to trace the issue. 3 Cross-verify dashboard data Use Query Console to independently confirm the raw row counts behind the Session 6 dashboard charts. Session 7 Checkpoint ✔ Simulated scheduler failure diagnosed via Scheduler Monitoring + Google Logs and resolved. ✔ Notification delivery confirmed; one stuck sync record identified and resolved. ✔ SAP payload confirmed processed in Legacy Queue Monitoring. ✔ APK rendering issue for kloRating traced (fixed or root-caused). ✔ Dashboard chart numbers cross-verified against raw data via Query Console. Enhancement delivered: Shifts the training from building features to operating and troubleshooting everything Sessions 1–6 put in place.
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 Duration: Full day

Create a client-specific child flavor using App Inheritance. Customize the child flavor without touching the base app via App Modification. Apply Customer Branding to the login page, menus, and headers. Version-control all Level 2 code in a Git repo. Migrate the fully enhanced application to QA and confirm every enhancement survived. What This Session Builds On The base Customer Complaints app is now feature-rich after Sessions 1–7. This final session prepares it for a real client rollout — a branded, inherited child flavor, migrated to QA.

The business is onboarding a new client, Acme, who needs their own complaint categories and branded login screen without touching the shared base app every other client depends on. Before go-live, someone has to confirm a departed developer's session is revoked and that the whole app still works correctly once it's moved to QA.

Create a client-specific variant without duplicating the whole app. # Action Detail 1 Create the child flavor New flavor customer_complaints_acme_<prid> inheriting from the base application. 2 Override safely Use App Modification to override complaint_type values for Acme's business categories, without changing the base flavor.

Make the child flavor visually distinct. # Action Detail 1 Update login/registration Modify the index file for the Acme child flavor with Acme's logo and welcome text. 2 Apply CSS Style menus and headers to match Acme's brand colors, scoped to .procify__customer_complaints_acme_<prid>.

Clean up before go-live. # Action Detail 1 Push code to Git Push all entity rules, controller code, and CSS written across Sessions 1–8 into a Git repo. 2 Review sessions Check Active Sessions for the app and revoke any stale developer sessions before go-live.
documents.s: Part C — Git Repo & Active Sessions

documents.t: Ship the enhanced application and prove every feature survived the move. # Action Detail 1 Release the flavor Release the Acme child flavor. 2 Migrate Run App Migration (Transport) from DEV to QA. 3 Full smoke test On QA, verify: escalation rule (S1), embedded timeline (S2), permissions/row-level auth (S3), offline sync (S4), workflow + notifications (S5), dashboard charts (S6), and Acme branding (S8) all work correctly. Session 8 Checkpoint ✔ Acme child flavor created, visually distinct, and functionally overridden without touching the base app. ✔ All Level 2 code version-controlled in Git. ✔ Stale developer sessions reviewed and revoked. ✔ Application migrated to QA with every Session 1–8 enhancement verified working end-to-end. Enhancement delivered: Delivers a branded, client-specific flavor without touching the shared base app, and proves every Session 1–8 enhancement survives the move to QA.
documents.s: Part D — App Migration to QA

Developer AI is an enhancement to the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform that enables users to build enterprise applications by describing their requirements in natural language. Instead of manually configuring application components, users can generate applications through a single prompt, significantly accelerating the application development process.

Developer AI is an AI-powered application development capability built on top of the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform. It transforms business requirements, provided in natural language, into a structured application design and automatically generates the foundational components required to build an enterprise application. Rather than requiring users to manually analyze requirements, design data models, create user interfaces, and configure application components, Developer AI automates these activities using artificial intelligence. This significantly reduces the time and effort involved in the initial stages of application development while ensuring consistency and alignment with business requirements.

When a user provides a business requirement through a prompt, Developer AI performs the following activities: Requirement Understanding Interprets the user's business requirement using Natural Language Processing (NLP). Identifies the business objective, workflows, business entities, users, and relationships. Extracts key functional and data requirements from the provided description. Business Analysis Converts the natural language requirement into structured business insights. Identifies business processes, modules, and system interactions. Determines the application's functional scope and required components. Data Model Generation Analyzes the business entities involved. Identifies attributes, primary keys, foreign keys, and relationships. Generates a normalized data model suitable for the application. Diagram Generation Based on the analyzed requirements, Developer AI automatically generates design artifacts such as: Entity Relationship (ER) Diagram Data Relationship Diagrams Business Process Flow Diagrams Other architecture and visualization diagrams required for application planning These diagrams provide a clear visual representation of the application's structure before development begins. Entity Creation Creates all required business entities. Defines fields, data types, validations, constraints, and relationships. Configures entities according to Procify platform standards. Screen Generation Developer AI automatically generates the application's user interface, including: Data Entry Screens List/Grid Views Detail Pages Forms Navigation structure The generated screens are mapped directly to the underlying business entities and workflows. Dashboard Generation Based on the application's business context, Developer AI creates dashboards containing: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Charts and Graphs Summary Cards Business Metrics Data Visualizations These dashboards provide users with meaningful insights into their business data from the outset. Application Foundation Creation After generating the business model, entities, screens, and dashboards, Developer AI produces the initial application structure within the Procify platform. This foundation serves as the starting point for further customization, refinement, and deployment.

Developer AI is designed to simplify and accelerate enterprise application development by leveraging Artificial Intelligence. It minimizes manual effort in the initial stages of development and enables organizations to transform business ideas into functional applications more efficiently.

Accelerates Application Development Converts business requirements into application components within minutes, significantly reducing development time. Reduces Manual Effort Eliminates the need for manually analyzing requirements, designing data models, and creating initial application structures. Converts Natural Language into Applications Enables users to describe business requirements in plain language, allowing AI to generate the application's foundation automatically. Automates Requirement Analysis Interprets business requirements and extracts key business entities, workflows, relationships, and functional requirements. Generates Design Artifacts Automatically Creates Entity Relationship (ER) diagrams, business process diagrams, and other visual models without manual intervention. Automatically Creates Business Entities Generates entities, attributes, relationships, validations, and data models based on the identified business requirements. Builds User Interface Components Automatically creates forms, screens, list pages, navigation, and dashboards, reducing UI development effort. Ensures Consistency and Standardization Produces applications following Procify platform standards and best practices, ensuring uniformity across projects. Improves Productivity Allows developers to focus on business logic and advanced customizations instead of repetitive setup tasks. Accelerates Time-to-Market Reduces the overall application development lifecycle, enabling organizations to deliver solutions faster. Minimizes Human Errors Automates repetitive design and configuration tasks, reducing the likelihood of manual mistakes. Supports Rapid Prototyping Enables quick creation of application prototypes that can be reviewed, refined, and enhanced based on stakeholder feedback. Enhances Collaboration Provides generated diagrams and structured application models that improve communication between business users, analysts, and developers. Scales with Business Needs Supports the rapid creation of applications of varying complexity while maintaining consistency and quality. Provides a Strong Application Foundation Generates the initial application structure, allowing developers to focus on enhancements, integrations, and business-specific customizations rather than starting from scratch.
documents.s: Key Reasons to Use Developer AI

documents.t: Adm version should be more than 1-0-47 Cockpit version should be more than 6-0-174
In User Collections, Developer AI needs to be enabled
In App Management, for the App, Developer AI needs to be enabled

We can access Developer AI from chatbot, the chatbot Icon is preset beside notification icon, in Homepage header Note: The chatbot icon is displayed only when Developer AI is enabled for the current landscape. If Developer AI is not enabled, the chatbot icon will not be visible. After click on this chatbot Icon, it will open the chatbot, from there to use the Developer AI, click on “Advanced Mode “ option, which will open the screen for using Developer AI

The Upload Business Requirement Document screen is the first step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this step, users select the target application, review the available AI token quota, and upload the Business Requirement Document (BRD) or Business Blueprint (BBP) that Developer AI will analyze to generate the application. Select Application​ The Select Application dropdown displays all applications, select application with Developer AI enabled the selected application acts as the target application where Developer AI will generate all the required components. All AI-generated artifacts, such as entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, and configurations, are created within the selected application. Ensure the correct application is selected before proceeding with document upload. Note :- 1. Developer AI not Enabled for Application If Developer AI is not enabled for the selected Application, It will show warning that Developer AI is not enabled for that application 2. Developer AI server is not available If the Developer AI Server is not running, a dialog will be displayed with the message: “Developer AI server is currently unavailable. Kindly contact the Administration team.” 3. BBP Build is triggered when other BBP build is in-progress in the same application If Build is triggered in the same application when other BBP Build is in-progress in the same application, then also the warning will come showing the BBP Build is already in progress Token Quota​ The Token Quota section displays the AI token consumption details for the selected user. A token represents a unit of text processed by the AI model. Every analysis performed on a BRD or BBP consumes tokens. The Token Quota panel provides the following information: Tokens Used – Total number of tokens consumed by Developer AI. Total Token Allocation – Maximum tokens allocated to the application. Remaining Tokens – Tokens still available for future AI operations. Usage Percentage – Visual progress bar showing the percentage of the allocated quota that has been consumed. Token Units​ Developer AI displays large token counts using abbreviated units: Unit Meaning Example K Thousand (1,000) 250K = 250,000 tokens M Million (1,000,000) 2.0M = 2,000,000 tokens Example If the Token Quota displays: 2.0M / 26.5M tokens 7% Used 24.5M Remaining It means: A total of 26.5 million tokens have been allocated. 2.0 million tokens have already been consumed. 24.5 million tokens are still available. Approximately 7% of the total token allocation has been utilized. Generate BBP​ The Generate BBP feature enables users to generate a Business Blueprint (BBP) by simply describing their application requirements in natural language. Instead of manually preparing a detailed BBP document, users can provide a high-level business description, and Developer AI automatically transforms it into a structured Business Blueprint. Upload BRD / BBP Document​ Once the application has been selected, upload the project documentation for analysis. Developer AI supports the following documents: Business Requirement Document (BRD) Business Blueprint (BBP) The document can be uploaded by: Dragging and dropping the file into the upload area. Selecting the file from the local system. Once the document is uploaded, Developer AI begins analyzing its contents to understand the business requirements and extract key information required to build the application. During this process, Developer AI identifies and generates: Business entities Functional requirements User roles Application screens Menu structure Business workflows Notifications Schedulers Dashboard requirements Homepage configuration Relationships between business objects The extracted information is then used to automatically generate the initial application structure within the selected Procify application. Preparing a BBP for Developer AI​ Developer AI expects the Business Blueprint (BBP) to follow a predefined structure for accurate analysis and application generation. If your existing BBP is not already in this format, it must be converted before uploading. To prepare a Developer AI-compatible BBP: Ensure you have the existing Business Blueprint (BBP) for your project. Refer to the Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt document (Prompt). Upload both: Your existing BBP. The Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt. Submit both documents to Claude for processing. The conversion prompt has been specifically designed and validated for Claude, and it is recommended not to use other AI models for this conversion. Claude will generate a new BBP that conforms to the standardized format required by Developer AI. Review the generated BBP to verify that the business requirements have been accurately converted. Upload the converted BBP using the Upload Business Requirement Document section to continue the application generation process. Once uploaded, Developer AI will analyze the standardized BBP and generate the application's foundational components, including entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, configurations, and other required artifacts.

The Analyze & Review tab is the second step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this stage, Developer AI processes the uploaded BRD or BBP and extracts all the business information required to build the application. The purpose of this step is to validate that the uploaded document has been successfully analyzed before proceeding with application generation. Once the document analysis is completed successfully and the extracted summary has been reviewed, click Open Dashboard to proceed to the detailed review screen. The Open Dashboard button opens the Review Extracted Information dashboard, where users can: Review all extracted business components in detail. Verify entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, schedulers, menu access, and homepage configuration. Modify, add, or remove extracted items as required. Validate the extracted information before proceeding to the Execution Plan stage. Review Extracted Information​ This section provides categorized access to all the information extracted from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Each category displays the number of items identified during the analysis, allowing users to review every component before proceeding with application generation. The available categories include: Entities – Displays the entities extracted from the document. Screens – Lists the application screens identified during analysis. Schedulers – Displays scheduled jobs or background processes. Functional Requirements – Shows the extracted business requirements. Notifications – Lists notification and alert configurations. User Roles – Displays user roles identified for role-based access control. Menu Access – Shows the application's navigation menu structure. Homepage – Displays the extracted homepage configuration. Out of Scope – Lists requirements identified as outside the application's scope. AI Visualize – Provides AI-generated visual representations of the extracted business information. Ask BBP – An AI-powered assistant that answers questions related to the uploaded BBP. Selecting a category displays its corresponding details in the main content area for review. Note: At present, manual addition, modification, or deletion of extracted components is not supported. The entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, and other components displayed on this screen are generated by Developer AI based on the uploaded BRD or BBP and are used as the foundation for application generation. Users can review the extracted information before proceeding to the next step.

Developer AI provides an option to export the extracted entity information for offline review or integration. Export to JSON​ The Export to JSON button downloads the extracted entity metadata in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format. The exported file contains structured information such as: Entity details Attributes Relationships Entity types Associated metadata The JSON format can be used for documentation, integration with external systems, or further processing. Export to TXT​ The Export to TXT option is currently not supported. Although the option is visible in the interface, exporting the extracted information in TXT format is not available in the current release and will be supported in a future version.

The Re-Analyze button allows users to run the document analysis again if changes have been made to the uploaded BRD or BBP, or if the extracted results need to be refreshed. When clicked, Developer AI: Reprocesses the uploaded document. Extracts the latest business requirements and application components. Updates the extracted entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, menu access, and other information.

The Mark All Review Completed button confirms that the extracted information has been reviewed and approved. Selecting this option indicates that: The extracted entities have been verified. Screens and functional requirements have been reviewed. User roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other extracted components have been validated. The application is ready to proceed to the next stage. Note: Marking the review as complete is mandatory before proceeding. If this step is not completed, an alert message will appear when you attempt to continue, prompting you to mark all reviews as completed before moving to the next stage.

The Execution Plan button navigates to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. After the review is completed, clicking Execution Plan opens the Execution Plan screen, where Developer AI displays the sequence of activities required to generate the application. The Execution Plan provides an overview of: Components to be generated. Order of execution. This serves as the final review before Developer AI begins generating the application.

The Refine BBP with AI feature is designed to allow users to improve or modify the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) using natural language instructions before proceeding with application generation. This option can be accessed by clicking the ✨ (AI Refine) button available on the Review Extracted Information screen.

Click the ✨ (AI Refine) button. The Refine BBP with AI dialog is displayed. What should AI change? text box, enter the required modifications or enhancements in natural language. Examples: Tighten the module scope. Add missing approval rules. Correct notification triggers. Add a new business entity. Update the workflow for order approval. Click Apply AI Changes. Developer AI is designed to analyze the provided instructions and update the extracted BBP accordingly. The refined information would then be reflected in the extracted components for further review before proceeding with application generation. Note: The Refine BBP with AI feature is currently not supported in the current release. Although the option is available in the interface, AI-based refinement of the extracted BBP is not yet functional and will be supported in a future release.

After clicking Execution Plan, the Review BBP Changes Before Build dialog is displayed. This screen provides a final summary of the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) before the application build process begins. The summary displays the number of: Existing in BBP – Components that were identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Added – New components that have been added during the review process. Updated – Components that have been modified before execution. The dialog also lists all the extracted application components, such as: Entities Screens Functional Requirements Notifications User Roles Other extracted artifacts This allows users to perform a final verification of the application metadata before proceeding with the build. Available Options Compare AI Changes – Displays a comparison between the original extracted information and any AI-generated changes (if applicable). Back to Review – Returns to the Review Extracted Information screen to make further changes or validations. Proceed to Execution Plan – Confirms the review and navigates to the Execution Plan screen, where the application generation workflow is initiated.

After clicking Proceed to Execution Plan, the Execution Selection screen is displayed. This screen allows users to review all extracted components and select the items that should be included in the application generation process. A summary at the top of the screen displays the total number of extracted components, including: Entities UI Screens Schedulers Workflows Notifications User Roles Menu Access Homepage Each category shows the number of items identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP.

The lower section displays the extracted components grouped by category. Each item is accompanied by a checkbox, allowing users to choose whether it should be included in the application build. Users can: Review the extracted entities and screens. Select or deselect individual components. Use the Select All option to include all available components for generation. Only the selected components will be considered during the application generation process.

After reviewing and selecting the required components, click Execute to start the application generation process. Developer AI begins generating the selected application components within the chosen Procify application. This includes creating the selected entities, screens, workflows, notifications, user roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other supported artifacts. Note: Ensure that all required components are selected before clicking Execute, as only the selected items will be included in the application generation process.

After clicking Execute, the Execution Progress screen is displayed. This screen tracks the progress of the application generation process and shows the status of each component being created. To begin generating the application, click Build Application.

The Build Application button initiates the application generation process based on the components selected in the Execution Plan. During the build process, Developer AI automatically creates and configures the selected application components, including: Business entities UI screens Value Helps Sample data Application roles Notifications Business rules Menus Homepage configuration Permissions Other supported application artifacts

As the build progresses, the Execution Progress section displays the status of each component. Each component is marked with one of the following statuses: In Progress – The component is currently being generated. Completed – The component has been successfully created. The progress cards provide a quick overview of the build status for each application component.

The Execution Log records every step performed during the application generation process. The log includes information such as: Analysis completion Entity creation Screen generation Business rule creation Sample data insertion Role creation Menu generation Homepage configuration Permission assignment Any warnings or errors encountered during the build The execution log helps users monitor the build process and troubleshoot issues if required.

When all selected components have been generated successfully, the status changes to Build Completed. A confirmation message indicates that the application has been successfully created within the selected Procify application. Users can then click Continue to proceed to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. Note :- Build Queue Notification When a BBP build is triggered for an application while another BBP build is already in progress for a different application, the new build request is not started immediately. Instead, it is automatically placed in a system-wide queue and will begin execution once the currently running build is completed. Build Already in Progress If a BBP build is triggered for an application that already has an active build in progress, Developer AI does not start a new build for the same application. Instead, it notifies the user that a build is already running and provides an option to view the current build progress. Click Yes, Show Progress to open the ongoing build progress screen, or click Cancel to close the notification

This step will allow users to configure application settings, assign users and roles, manage permissions, customize branding, and define deployment-related configurations before publishing the application.
This step will allow users to validate the generated application, perform publish readiness checks, and publish the application to the target environment.
This step will allow users to generate AI-powered test cases and execute automated Playwright tests to validate the generated application.
This step will allow users to generate AI-powered technical documentation, user guides, configuration guides, and downloadable project documentation for the generated application.
This step will allow users to review the final application generation summary, verify the completed workflow, and conclude the Developer AI application generation process.

Entities After the application is generated, all the business entities created by Developer AI are automatically available in the Data Studio. These entities form the core data model of the generated application and can be reviewed and further configured as needed. The left navigation panel displays the list of all generated entities. Selecting an entity opens its complete configuration, where you can review its properties, relationships, business rules, workflows, access control, and other metadata. Note: If the generated entities are not immediately visible in the Data Studio, refresh the application or browser. The entities will be displayed once the latest metadata is loaded. Screens Developer AI automatically generates the required application pages based on the uploaded BRD/BBP. These pages provide the user interface for interacting with the generated business entities and application features. The generated pages are available in the Page Builder and can be reviewed, customized, or enhanced using the standard Procify page designer. In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following pages: p_homepage_001 – The application's landing page that provides users with the initial view after logging in. p_dashboard_001 – Displays the application's dashboard, providing a consolidated view of key information, widgets, and business insights. p_delivery_mgmt – The Delivery Management page used to create, view, update, and manage delivery-related transactions. Role & Users The roles and users generated by Developer AI can be viewed from the Roles & Users section under the Details tab of the generated application in App Management. This section allows you to review the user roles and user assignments created for the application. Homepage Log in using one of the users created in the Roles & Users section. After successful login, the application opens the Homepage generated by Developer AI. The homepage displayed corresponds to the configuration defined in the Homepage component during the application generation process. It serves as the application's landing page and provides users with quick access to the generated modules, dashboards, and navigation menus based on their assigned role and permissions. Dashboard Developer AI automatically generates the application dashboard based on the requirements defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP. The generated dashboard provides users with a consolidated view of key business information, metrics, and navigation components relevant to the application. It is designed to offer quick access to important data and frequently used features immediately after login. The dashboard created by Developer AI can be accessed from the Dashboard menu within the generated application and can be further customized using the standard Procify dashboard designer to meet specific business requirements. Note: The layout, widgets, and overall design of the generated dashboard are determined by Developer AI based on its analysis of the uploaded BBP or BRD. Dashboard generation is AI-driven, and users cannot control or define the dashboard layout by providing screenshots or sample designs. To influence the generated dashboard, include clear and detailed dashboard requirements within the BBP or BRD. Menu Developer AI automatically generates the application's navigation menu based on the modules, screens, and user workflows defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP. The generated menu provides users with organized navigation to access the application's features. Menu items are created based on the business requirements and are assigned appropriate access according to the generated user roles and permissions. In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following menu items: Home – The default landing page that provides users with quick access to the application. My Deliveries – A module for managing and viewing delivery-related transactions. Dashboard – Provides access to the application's dashboard, displaying key business insights and summary information.
